lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Independent application A: short medium and long goals

objective: Learners convert invented short, medium, and long goals into monthly requirements and test the combined plan against available funds.
scenario: Xanthe is an invented eighth grader planning three pretend goals: $1,800.00 in 6 months, $9,000.00 in 36 months, and $24,000.00 in 120 months. She has $700.00 a month available. All figures are invented.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Convert Xanthe's invented short goal, $1,800.00 in 6 months, into a monthly amount.

prompts.text: What monthly amount does the short goal require?

tasks.directions: Convert Xanthe's medium and long goals the same way, keeping each requirement separate.

prompts.text: What monthly amount does the $9,000.00 goal require over 36 months?
What monthly amount does the $24,000.00 goal require over 120 months?

tasks.directions: Total Xanthe's three monthly requirements and compare them with the $700.00 available.

prompts.text: What do the three goals require each month?
How much short is the monthly amount available?

tasks.directions: Only the short goal has a hard deadline.

prompts.text: Recommend which of Xanthe's timelines to extend to close the $50.00 gap, and explain why the horizon of a goal affects how much it can be stretched.

remediation: If a learner divides in the wrong direction, restate each of Xanthe's goals as sharing the total across the months and check the units of the answer.
extension: Ask the learner to extend exactly one of Xanthe's timelines so the plan fits $700.00, and to show the new figures.
